# Activation Plan Functions

Plans a document's party channels, approval operations, access monitoring, optional terms negotiation and activation dispatch policy. `plan` returns contract contributions and initial state; returning a plan does not itself establish installation, participant acceptance or activation. Inherited functions maintain activation when the installed handlers execute.

## Configuration

`configuration` reads `/clauseRuntime/work/candidate/{clauseKey}/parameters`. Runtime functions use `/activation` and `/clauses/activation/parameters` in the executing document. There are no configurable data bindings in the supplied definition.

- `parties` must be a nonempty object keyed by party role. Each party needs `lead/channel`; optional `representatives` supply additional channels. Party and representative keys must be nonempty text without `.`, `/`, `~` or `__`. Lead channels use the role name; representative channels use `role__representative`.
- `required` defaults to all configured party roles and identifies whose approval is needed. `revision` defaults to `1`. Initial `approved` and `accessRequests` are empty objects.
- `accessPaths` defaults to `[]` and identifies embedded access documents. `readers` defaults to `{}` and supplies additional reader-key groups. Party `readerKeys` and representative `readerKeys` supply their corresponding groups, overriding same-named entries in `readers`.
- `frozen` defaults to `false`; initial roster freezing also applies when `/partyRosterFrozen` is exactly `true`. `allowNewParties` defaults to `false` and controls direct additions through `updateParty`. The separate approved-admission helper requires nonempty `admission/approvers`.
- `preActivationOperations` and `preActivationChannels` default to `[]`. The plan also allows the planned roster's `approve_<role>` and `updateParty_<role>` operations before activation, plus any generated negotiation operations.
- `negotiation/allowedPaths` defaults to `[]`. Nonempty configuration enables negotiation planning. Paths must be distinct absolute paths with nonempty segments and no `~`. They cannot start under `clauses`, `contracts`, `activation`, `clauseRuntime`, `type`, `name` or `description`, or equal or descend from a configured access path. Initialization requires each selected field to exist and be text, integer, double or boolean.

Negotiation additionally requires at least one negotiator, the document's `/type`, and a candidate clause `negotiationDefinition/functions` containing `proposeChanges`. Negotiators are `required`, defaulting to all roster roles. The plan supplies a `validTermsCandidate` matcher for the document's declared type.

Planning reuses an existing unmanaged channel only when its definition matches exactly; otherwise it rejects with `ACTIVATION_CHANNEL_CONFLICT`. `validateTransition` rejects direct changes to this clause with `USE_ACTIVATION_PARTY_OPERATIONS`. While negotiation is configured and activation has never been recorded, changes to the entire clause set are rejected with `NEGOTIATION_POLICY_LOCKED`.

## Access, readiness and dispatch

For each roster transport matching `Timeline Channel`, access checking requires one same-provider `Timeline Access` document containing that exact timeline and at least one allowed key from every reader group. Keys within a group are alternatives; different groups must each be covered. This check does not combine partial coverage across access documents. Transports matching `External Channel` bypass that transport's access-document test.

`computeState` checks access for the current roster together with pending additions whose `expectedRevision` matches the activation revision. It records the same access result in `functional` and `accessReady`. `termsAccepted` requires every `required` party's approval and unchanged values at all recorded terms paths. `active` additionally requires access readiness and an unset `closed` flag.

The maintained `status` distinguishes:

- `WAITING_FOR_ACCESS`: access requirements are unmet before any recorded activation.
- `SUSPENDED_ACCESS`: access requirements are unmet after a recorded activation.
- `AWAITING_ACCEPTANCE`: access is ready, but required approvals or agreement with recorded terms are missing.
- `ACTIVE`: access and acceptance conditions hold and the document is not closed.
- `CLOSED`: `closed` is true, taking precedence over the other statuses.

`reason` is `PARTICIPANT_ACCESS_MISSING`, `ACCEPTANCE_REQUIRED` or empty according to access and acceptance; it is not a separate closure reason. `everActivated` preserves whether a committed state has ever been active. Missing state is unknown; initialization defaults apply only after initialization executes.

`Clauses Initialized` and embedded `Timeline Access Updated` events trigger refresh. Refresh initializes terms when needed, commits readiness and updates pending access-request readiness. A first activation emits `Document Activated`; loss of access from an active state emits `Document Access Suspended`. `Document Access Restored` is emitted when previously unavailable access permits an already-activated document to become active again. Access recovery alone need not restore activity if acceptance conditions no longer hold.

The dispatch policy admits initialization and recognized embedded access-control deliveries even while ordinary work is blocked. Other deliveries require initialized activation, `accessReady`, a fresh access check and an open document. It then permits configured pre-activation operations or non-external pre-activation channels; remaining work requires business readiness.

A registered admission-consent operation can also pass before activation when its item is `admission_pending` and its token, admission reference, activation revision, invoking channel, installed operation and party lead-channel identities match the registration. This exception does not bypass access or closure checks and does not itself establish consent.

A denied delivery skips its handlers. External inputs are still consumed and checkpointed, so becoming active later does not replay them. Passing this policy does not override another installed policy or the operation's own guards.

## Party approval, updates and admission

`approve_<role>` is bound to that party's lead channel. Approval requires `call/requireExactDocumentVersion` to be true, the current activation `revision` and valid participant access. With negotiation enabled, `termsRef` is required; any supplied `termsRef` must match `/activation/terms/ref`. Representatives cannot substitute for the party lead in this approval function. An already-recorded approval returns without another acceptance event. A new approval commits state and emits `Terms Accepted`; one party's acceptance does not necessarily activate the document.

`updateParty_<role>` also requires exact-document review and a party lead, and rejects a frozen roster. Its `party` input defaults to the invoking role; `replacement` needs `lead/channel` and valid representative names. A lead can replace its own party or, when `allowNewParties` permits, add an explicitly named new party. It cannot replace another existing party. The proposed roster must pass access checks and avoid unrelated contract-name collisions. Success rebuilds roster contracts, clears approvals, increments `revision` and emits `Party Changed`. A direct addition also appends the new role to `required`; no revision argument is required by this public input.

Subject to dispatch, `Party Addition Requested` starts access preparation. Stale-revision and already-recorded requests are ignored. Supplied `accessDocuments` are keyed by party or representative transport. They must preserve the native provider-owned access policy and carry initialization and provider-history evidence. Installation accepts one to sixteen documents per call, deduplicates by original document identity and registers refresh channels under `/partyAccess`.

Missing coverage can emit `Party Access Update Requested` for specific existing-party transports. These events request an external permission change; they grant neither access nor participant consent. A request's `ready` result checks coverage of every transport of its parent party. Provider-confirmed executed access state remains the permission evidence.

`admitApprovedParties` separately commits roster additions. It requires an unfrozen roster, matching revision, an admission policy, valid main-party identities and established access. Existing roles must preserve their lead channel and primary reader-key set. An unchanged roster returns `duplicate`; a changed roster installs contracts, increments the activation revision and emits `Party Changed` with kind `Participants admitted`. This helper does not automatically add admitted roles to `required`, and its supplied body does not show how upstream admission approvals or consent are collected.

## Terms and negotiation

`initializeTerms` records selected scalar values in `terms/fields`. `terms/definition` identifies the remaining initial document after separating those fields and excluding configured access documents, access configuration and parties' own `readerKeys`. `terms/ref` identifies the resulting definition and field values. Initialization sets `termsRevision` and `negotiation/revision` to `1`, marks negotiation editable and creates empty proposal, history and outcome objects.

Changes to the roster or required roles renew the terms reference, increment `termsRevision` and clear a pending proposal with outcome `AUTHORITY_CHANGED`. They also clear approvals when negotiation is configured. An approval that reaches active state marks negotiation uneditable and clears any pending proposal with outcome `SUPERSEDED`.

For each negotiator, the plan creates `proposeChanges_<role>`, `proposeAndActivate_<role>`, `activate_<role>`, `withdrawProposal_<role>`, `rejectProposal_<role>` and `withdrawAcceptance_<role>`. These delegate to corresponding `Public` functions in the clause-supplied negotiation library.

Proposal inputs carry the current `baseTermsRef`, a unique `proposalId` and a nonempty `changes` list. Each `Term Change` identifies an allowed `path` and a selected `replacement` subject to that term's definition. `supersedes` identifies the current proposal being replaced. Selection inputs carry `termsRef`; `proposalId` is omitted for current terms and included for selected proposed terms. Withdrawal and rejection requests identify the selected proposal by `proposalId`.

The delegated negotiation bodies are not supplied, so their detailed acceptance, withdrawal and rejection effects are not established here. Likewise, the shown runtime interprets `closed` but supplies no operation that sets it. Operation availability alone establishes neither a viewer's authority nor a personal obligation.
